Judgment :

1. Original Respondent No. 2 in MACP No. 63/2010 hereby takes exception to the judgment and award dated 06.04.2016 passed by learned MACT, Udgir, which was a claim set up by heirs of Dinkar, seeking compensation on account of road accident dated 14.03.2010.
2. Brief background of the claim petition is that, on 14.03.2010 deceased Dinkar was riding his bicycle.

In the vicinity of village Vilegaon motorcycle bearing no. MH-14-W-4257 came in excessively high speed in opposite direction and gave dash to Dinkar, who suffered grievous fatal injuries and while undergoing treatment he succumbed.
3. On account of death due to involvement of motor vehicle, his heirs filed above accident claim petition by invoking Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act urging compensation on various heads.
That time claim was sought from one Sunil Shinde, present Appellant Shriniwas in the capacity of rider - owner of the motorcycle.
Claimants got deleted name of Sunil and instead inserted name of Rajkumar More, owner of the offending vehicle.

After contest and on the analyzing the oral and documentary evidence, claim petition was allowed directing Respondent Nos.1A, Respondent No. 2 - present Appellant, Respondent No.3 to jointly and severally pay compensation to the tune of Rs.9,85,000/- with interest.
PAGE 2 OF 6 FA-2588.odt 4.
Feeling aggrieved by the above award, original Respondent No.2 has come up in Appeal assailing the above award by raising a ground that, on the day of accident he was not the owner of the motorcycle.
He had already sold it to Rajkumar.
However, such contentions of Applicant are not considered by learned Tribunal and rather liability has directly been saddled on Appellant, even when there was no concern with the offending vehicle.
That, neither his written statement nor plea therein has been considered and appreciated.
He further pointed out that, though crime was registered against Appellant No.2, he ultimately, on full fledged trial, came to be acquitted.

5. Learned Counsel for Respondents submits that, there is no dispute that, claimants had on their own accord deleted original Respondent No.1 - Sunil Shinde and instead 1-A i.e. Rajkumar More was brought on record as Respondent.

He expressed his primary concern with compensation amount i.e.
whether this by A-1 or jointly with other Respondents.
6.
In the light of above submissions, papers on record are put to scrutiny.
It is emerging that, MACP No. 63/2010 is at the instance of wife, two daughters and son of Dinkar Naikwad, who had met road traffic accident on 14.03.2010.
There is no dispute to this extent.

There is further no dispute that,

sentences.text: Present Appellants are shown as Respondent Nos.2 & 3.
However, they too was shown to be impleaded as owner and driver of the vehicle.
The third Respondent is the rider of the offending vehicle.
7. It is a matter of record that, offending motorcycle was seized from the spot while the rider was not available there.

Initially, present Appellant No.1 was shown to be owner but he has contested the impleadment primarily on the ground that, though he was shown as original owner, he had sold the vehicle to 1-A Rajkumar More and vehicle stood in the name of said person on the day of accident.

To buttress such contention, learned Counsel invited attention of this Court to Exhibit 36 and 37,
which are RC particular and part of record.
On studying the same, it does emerge that, initially vehicle stood in the name of Sunil Shinde in May, 2006.
However, motorcycle is shown to be transferred to Rajkumar Anand More as per R.T.O's order dated 24/26.04.2007.

Accident in question has admittedly taken place on 14.03.2010.
8.

Going by above exhibited documents, there is reason to hold PAGE 4 OF 6 FA-2588.odt that, on the date of accident offending motorcycle stood in the name of 1-A and, therefore, when present Appellants by way of written statement Exhibit 21 has specifically taken up a plea to the above extent, learned Tribunal ought to have considered the same and after framing issue to that extent in the light of pleading, matter ought to have decided the same.
However, it does not seem to have so happen.
On the contrary, mere finding is recorded that, there is no evidence and so said pleadings cannot be accepted for want of papers.
Above exhibits are not taken into account by learned Tribunal, which has resulted it in fixing liability on present Appellants and others.

9. Apart from above, learned Counsel for Appellants has placed on record judgment dated 06.05.2015 passed by learned JMFC, Deoni, by which present Appellant No. 2 was shown to be charge-sheeted has already been acquitted.

On going through the copy of judgment passed in STCC No. 18/2010 learned JMFC seems to have recorded a specific finding in paragraph 32 that,
prosecution failed to prove that accused Bhagwan i.e. present Appellant No. 2 was not driving the motorcycle on the date of the accident. Hence, he too cannot be saddled with liability.
10. To sum up, here there is documentary evidence in support of pleadings before learned Tribunal that, present Appellant No. 1 was not the owner of the offending motorcycle on the date of accident and it was PAGE 5 OF 6 FA-2588.odt rather 1-A Rajkumar More and, therefore, finding to that extent passed by learned Tribunal is required to be interfered with.
11.
In view of above discussion, Appellants succeed.

Hence, the following order:
ORDER (a) First Appeal is allowed.
